Trajectory number 1 simulates the interceptor with 8 segments and trajectory number 
2 simulates the target with 4 segments. This problem is set up similarly to previous 
examples so only the differences are discussed. 
Optimization 
The main feature of this problem is the use of optimization to calculate the shape of 
the intercept trajectory. Segments 2 and 5 in the first trajectory, representing the bum 
times of the first and second stages, have guidance rules with angle-of-attack time 
histories. All of the angle-of-attack values are optimization parameters. The opti- 
mization procedure varies these angle-of-attack values to achieve maximum veloc- 
ity at impact. Maximum velocity is used instead of maximum range because it con- 
verges faster and gives similar results. 
The other optimization parameter is the initial longitude of the interceptor. The target 
is launched from a zero longitude and latitude heading east. The interceptor is 
launched from zero latitude heading west, but its initial longitude is unknown. Its ini- 
tial longitude needs to be as far east as possible and still intercept the target 90 se- 
conds after launch.
